shots.phrase: Begin by framing Introduction to Thesis Preparation as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results.

Students work with a supervising faculty member to complete their undergraduate thesis proposal, and do additional background preparation (for example, programming, study, exercises, and analysis) for the subject area and specific problem(s) to be addressed in a thesis.
List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion.
Now define Defining the Research Problem precisely enough that another learner could test the definition.
A research project narrows a question, reviews literature, defines a reproducible method, evaluates results, and communicates for the intended audience.
Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them.
With the foundation in place, examine how Methodology and Reproducibility operates in a concrete sequence.
Consider this worked case: Students document exact software versions, dataset sources, and step-by-step procedures for their thesis experiment.
The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence.
Next, compare the choices involved in Ethical Computing Standards and make the decision criteria explicit.
Consider this worked case: Students include a section in their proposal detailing how they will anonymize student data and obtain necessary permissions.
Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts.
Apply Responsible Technical Communication to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition.
Consider this worked case: Students structure their proposal to clearly separate their novel hypothesis from established literature findings.
Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step.
Examine the tradeoffs in Results and Limitations, including what improves and what becomes more difficult.
Results should be reported accurately rather than selected to create a misleading conclusion.
State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable.
Stress-test the reasoning around Research Integrity and Plagiarism with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome.
Authors should preserve research integrity and avoid plagiarism, fabrication, and falsification.
Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds.
Use Supervisor Deliverables and Planning to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action.
Additional deliverables set by the advisor are also required (for example, source code, bibliographies, notes, presentations, etc.
Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause.
Connect Evaluation Criteria and Quality Standards to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system.
Professionals should strive to achieve high quality in both processes and products.
Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations.
Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis.
At the end of the semester, a thesis proposal must be submitted for approval to the advisor.
For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step.
